subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a cron-scoped tool-policy config surface, make cron runs inherit subagent tool policy, or intentionally leave cron restrictions limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow`?
rationale: The choice defines a public config and security-boundary contract for scheduled autonomous runs, and automation should not choose the default, inheritance, or upgrade behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with precedence, docs, schema/type coverage, and upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Reuse `tools.subagents.tools` for cron sessions, reducing config surface but coupling two distinct session classes and risking upgrade surprises.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Leave cron restrictions to `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery mitigations, accepting the current operator ergonomics and defense-in-depth gap.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with precedence, docs, schema/type coverage, and upgrade-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current blame and prior review signal for the schema/tool-policy boundary decision.
